audit_action.format: A dotted, lower-case action name, for example pull_request.merge.

pull_request_review.submit.meaning: A pull request review was submitted.

protected_branch.update_admin_enforced.meaning: Enforcement of a branch protection rule for repository admins was turned on or off.

protected_branch.update_pull_request_rev.meaning: Which accounts required pull request reviews apply to was changed on a branch.

protected_branch.update_required_status_.meaning: Which accounts required status checks apply to was changed on a branch.

examples.note: @timestamp and created_at carry this same value on the same record
on the pull_request.create sample, equal to actor_id by coincidence, not by rule

values.admin: The member is an organization owner.
values.billing_manager: A member restricted to billing management, with no code or admin access.

values.pending: The user has been invited but has not yet accepted.

gh_user_account_type.format: One fixed word naming the account's kind.

examples.note: an ordinary GitHub account, seen on github:cloud:user
the repository owner is itself an organization, seen on a Dependabot alert's repository.owner

alert_state.format: One fixed word, the set depends on the alert type (see the concept description).

values.dismissed: A person dismissed the alert without fixing it (code-scanning, Dependabot).
values.fixed: The underlying issue was fixed (code-scanning, Dependabot).
values.resolved: The alert was closed out (secret-scanning; resolution names how).
values.auto_dismissed: GitHub automatically dismissed the alert, for example because the dependency was removed (Dependabot).

alert_dismissed_reason.format: A fixed phrase; code-scanning uses spaces, Dependabot uses underscores.

false positive.meaning: The finding does not describe a real issue.

won't fix.meaning: A real issue the team has decided not to fix.

used in tests.meaning: The flagged code only runs in tests.

inaccurate.meaning: The alert does not accurately describe the issue.

no_bandwidth.meaning: The team does not have time to address it now.

not_used.meaning: The vulnerable code path is not used.

tolerable_risk.meaning: The risk is accepted as tolerable.

rule_severity.format: One fixed word from the linter's own scale.

values.false_positive: The detected string was not actually a secret.
values.wont_fix: A real secret the team decided not to revoke.
values.used_in_tests: The secret only ever ran in tests.

values.active: GitHub's own check found the secret still works.
values.inactive: GitHub's own check found the secret no longer works.
values.unknown: GitHub did not check, or the secret type is not checkable.

values.runtime: The dependency is used when the application runs.
values.development: The dependency is only used while developing or testing.

vendor_label.format: A short constant string; the literal depends on the container (see the binding note).

api_link.format: An https URL, GitHub's own hypermedia link.

examples.note: the GHES-doc HOSTNAME placeholder, left unsubstituted in the Dependabot sample as vendor-published

branch_protection_policy_flag.format: true or false; which policy toggle depends on the binding's column.

branch_protection_enforcement_level.format: Not enumerated here; GitHub's audit log names one update event per column (protected_branch.update_*_enforcement_level). No sample or page read for this pack states the literal value set.

branch_ref_name.format: A branch, tag or ref name string.

event_object_name.format: Free text; varies by the action recorded.

event_object_description.format: Free text; varies by the action recorded.

gh_repo_visibility.format: Not enumerated here; no sample or page read for this pack confirms the literal value set.

origin_repo_full_name.format: owner/repo, the same shape as repo_full_name.

pull_request_url.format: A GitHub REST API or web UI URL for one pull request.

ruleset_name.format: Free text, the ruleset's own display name.

disabled.meaning: Rules are defined but not enforced.

evaluate.meaning: Rules run and are logged without blocking anything.

Repository.meaning: The ruleset was created at the repository level.

Organization.meaning: The ruleset was created at the organization level.

Enterprise.meaning: The ruleset was created at the enterprise level.

branch.meaning: The ruleset's rules apply to matching branches.

tag.meaning: The ruleset's rules apply to matching tags.

push.meaning: The ruleset's rules apply to pushes.

repository.meaning: The ruleset's rules apply at the repository level.

ruleset_component_id.format: A positive integer, unique within its ruleset.

ruleset_rule_type.format: One fixed word naming a rule kind.

required_linear_history.meaning: Requires a linear commit history, no merge commits.

required_deployments.meaning: Requires status checks to pass in named deployment environments.

required_signatures.meaning: Requires signed commits on matching refs.

pull_request.meaning: Requires a pull request before merging into matching refs.

required_status_checks.meaning: Requires the listed status checks to pass before merging.

non_fast_forward.meaning: Blocks force pushes to matching refs.

commit_message_pattern.meaning: Restricts commit messages to a pattern.

commit_author_email_pattern.meaning: Restricts commit author emails to a pattern.

committer_email_pattern.meaning: Restricts committer emails to a pattern.

branch_name_pattern.meaning: Restricts branch names to a pattern.

tag_name_pattern.meaning: Restricts tag names to a pattern.

file_path_restriction.meaning: Restricts file paths pushed to matching refs.

max_file_path_length.meaning: Caps the length of a file path pushed to matching refs.

file_extension_restriction.meaning: Restricts file extensions pushed to matching refs.

max_file_size.meaning: Caps the size of a file pushed to matching refs.

workflows.meaning: Requires the listed GitHub Actions workflows to pass before merging.

code_scanning.meaning: Requires the listed code scanning results before merging.

copilot_code_review.meaning: Requires a Copilot code review before merging.
